notes: Spent clicks and credits clearing tags, then reran HQ to see the same cards and went broke. With no killer it ran into the known Anansi twice, lost its whole grip, then ran it again with 2 cards and was flatlined.

Won slowly against a corp that was broke for many turns, mostly by rerunning HQ into the same Jackson Howard over and over. It set up Security Testing and seldom used it well, and ran elsewhere while an agenda in Server 3 got scored.
Good early pressure on open R&D. From turn 7 it took 1 credit with every click for 11 turns, reaching 57 credits, and never ran while the corp scored naked or barely-iced remotes to win.
Won with steady R&D/HQ pressure but let Drafter fire on every run. It wasted credits on pointless 'install from heap' breaker actions and kept rerunning HQ into the same Rashida.
Sensible: an early Obokata steal, a breaker found, and steady R&D pressure. The middle turns were passive draw/credit turns, and it spent a lot on tag removal.
After two bounced runs it only clicked for credits up to 36 and never ran again while agendas were advanced over several turns in Server 1. It paid 4 for a pointless Paperclip heap install.

The corp was at 0 credits and 0 cards from turn 5, yet the runner made one R&D run per turn at most. It kept rerunning Archives to hit the same Cyberdex and took 1 credit per click, which dragged out an easy win.
Hoarded over 70 credits by taking 1 credit per click for about 18 turns and never ran HQ or R&D. The corp scored a Hostile Takeover and three Project Atlases from remotes it left alone.
Reached 49 credits by taking 1 credit per click and never ran R&D or HQ. It ignored the agendas being advanced over several turns in Server 1, and the corp won uncontested.
Good, aggressive R&D pressure won by turn 9. Minor oddities: facechecking Surveyor with no link, and using Zer0 in a way that trashed a freshly installed Black Orchestra.
Won, but repeatedly pumped Black Orchestra without breaking Fairchild, losing it and taking core damage several times. Twice it ran elsewhere while agendas in Server 2 were scored.
Won with persistent R&D pressure. It wasted many credits on pointless Paperclip/MKUltra heap installs and on pumping Black Orchestra without breaking Mausolus, and it spent several clicks on tags.

Sat on 20-34 credits taking 1 credit per click while Megaprix and GFI were installed and scored in remotes. It then ran Server 3 four times in one turn into an Ansel that it could not break and that stopped every steal.
Ran Archives about 60 times, always declining the same Obokata, and did nothing else for 15 turns. The corp scored three Send a Messages without the runner ever contesting them.

Reasonable asset trashing early, but it let Send a Message be advanced over two turns uncontested. It then ran a 3-ice remote with the known Anansi behind it and no killer, and was flatlined through Loki.

After early HQ reruns seeing the same cards, it mostly took 1 credit per click up to 35 and never installed breakers. It made only occasional asset-trashing runs and never contested the Server 6 agendas that won the game.
Solid aggressive game against a poor corp: it hit R&D and the remote at the right times and won turn 11. Its economy was thin and it spent some clicks on tag removal, but no major mistakes.

Early multi-access R&D pressure was fine, but its economy collapsed to 0 credits. It repeatedly ran into the known Komainu with no money to break it, shredding its grip until a Snare access flatlined it.

A fast start to 6 points was followed by a 20-turn grind at 0-3 credits after MaxX emptied the stack. It made many repeat empty Archives runs and paid for pointless heap installs before finally winning on turn 27.
After early R&D runs it took 1 credit per click for five turns up to 26 and never found a way past one Vanilla. Agendas were scored from Server 1 uncontested, and it never ran HQ.
